transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because things have been pretty stressful lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I just haven't quite been myself. 

I mean, I’m holding it together at work fine, but at home and with my coursework, I’m just... I'm a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I’m used to being. And I've noticed I've started skipping the things that usually keep my head clear. I haven't been fishing, haven't touched my woodworking, and I even stopped going to the first-aid workshops I usually like. I just figured I should probably talk to someone to get a handle on it.
Do you feel this stress began after your father-in-law moved in with you?

Yeah, it really did. He moved in about four months ago, and I'd say I started noticing the strain within the first couple of months. It just took a little bit of time for the new home routines and the caregiving demands to really settle in, and once they did, that's when the stress started catching up with me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down. It's more just... feeling tense and on edge all the time, you know? Like my patience is just wearing thin, but I don't feel sad or anything like that.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things besides your father-in-law living with you?

No, not really. It's pretty much just focused on the situation at home. I mean, I don't sit around worrying about my job or bills or anything like that more than I usually would. It's really just the new routine and the extra demands with my father-in-law that are keeping me so on edge.
Has this stress been interfering with your ability to manage things at home or keep up with your coursework?

Well, my regular EMT work is going fine, I'm still doing all my shifts. But... yeah, I have fallen behind on some of my paramedic coursework. It's just hard to find the time and focus right now. And I've also stopped showing up consistently for the community first-aid workshops I usually help out with. I've just kind of had to drop the ball on that extra stuff to keep my head above water at home.
Would you say this stress feels stronger than you would normally expect yourself to have in this situation?

I mean, I don't know if it's stronger than normal. It's a lot to deal with, having him move in and need so much help. I think anyone would be stressed out by it. I don't really have a baseline for what's normal to feel right now, it's just... it's just hard.
Has this situation caused serious problems in your home life or relationships?

I wouldn't say it's caused serious problems with my marriage or anything like that. We're both just really tired. Like I mentioned a minute ago, the main issue is really just how it's affecting my extra responsibilities. I'm still getting to my regular EMT shifts fine, but... yeah, I've fallen behind on my paramedic classes and had to stop going to those community first-aid workshops. I just don't have the bandwidth for much else outside of work and helping out at home right now.
Would you say your level of stress feels out of proportion to what most people would feel in this situation?

I mean, I think I just answered that, but... no, I don't think it's out of proportion. Like I said, it's a lot to take on, having him move in and need all this care. I think most people would be pretty stressed out trying to juggle all of this. It just makes sense that I'm feeling this way.
